newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jauch & Huebener has no comment on US broker deal.
newsitem.headline: Jauch & Huebener has no comment on US broker deal.

text.p: German insurance broker Jauch & Huebener declined to comment on Wednesday on the news of the planned merger between brokers Marsh & McLennan and Johnson & Higgins.

Johnson & Higgins and Jauch & Huebener are major partners in the Unison insurance broker network. Unison member companies are active in more than 200 offices in over 70 countries. Together they have more than 14,000 staff.

Jauch & Huebener handles all its international business via Unison. But Marsh & McLennan, the new Johnson & Higgins partner, owns Germany's second-largest broking firm, Gradmann Holler, which is a rival of market leader Jauch & Huebener.
"We will discuss consequences for Unison next week in New York," Christian Dahms, spokesman for the managing partners of Germany's largest broker, told Reuters.
In 1995, Jauch & Huebener had commission and fee income of 311 million marks and 1,426 staff.
Gradmann Holler has some 800 staff and income of around 210 million marks.
Marsh & McLennan chief executive A.J.C. Smith told Reuters that the future of Johnson & Higgins' Unison partnerships was still unclear.
"We really haven't been able to address that thoroughly yet," Smith told analysts.

"Clearly there are some fine firms in Unison that we would be happy to be associated with. In other places, Marsh & McLennan already has very substantial operations and it would perhaps not make sense for it to be larger," he said.
Other members of Unison include Gras Savoye, based in Paris, Gil y Carvajal, based in Madrid, and Mees & Zoonen, based in Rotterdam.
